title: LC-MSMS analysis of immunoprecipitated JunB-FLAG from HAP1 ADO KO cells
projectDescription: Define the N-terminal acetylation status of human JunB in siCTRL, siNAA10 or siNAA20 treated HAP1 ADO KO cells.
sampleProcessingProtocol: HAP1 ADO KO cells transfected with siNAA10, siNAA20 or non-targeting control siRNA. After 48 hours, the cells were split in a 1:2 ratio and incubated for 6-7 h before transfecting the cells with 6 µg pRP/JUNB-FLAG-P2A-EGFP plasmid. 24 h post transfection, cells were harvested and lysed. JUNB-FLAG was immunoprecipitated using Flag-Trap Agarose beads. IP samples were further processed for LC-MS/MS analysis. IP beads were resuspended in incubation buffer supplemented with DTT for 10 min at 95 °C. Cysteines were alkylated by CAA. Protein samples were digested overnight using Arg-C. The digestion was stopped by TFA. Peptides were desalted using Pierce C18 spin tips and eluted in 0.1% formic acid (FA) and 70 % acetonitrile (ACN). The samples were further frozen at -80 °C, before drying the peptides using a speed vac evaporator. Finally, the dried peptides were resuspended in 2 % ACN and 0.5 % FA. The peptide samples were analysed by LC-MS/MS. About 0.5 µg peptide sample was injected into an Ultimate 3000 RSLC system (Thermo Scientific, Sunnyvale, California, USA) connected online to a Orbitrap Eclipse mass  spectrometer (Thermo Scientific, Bremen, Germany) equipped with EASY-spray nanoelectrospray ion source source (Thermo Scientific). (See paper for further details).
dataProcessingProtocol: Thermo Proteome Discoverer 2.5.0.400 was used to analyse the LC-MS/MS data.
